description: Quad Cortex block names and parameters onto Pedaleira kinds. Built from public sources only (docs/import.md, 'Sources'). Nothing here has been checked against a dump from a real unit yet: every model is verified false, and a parameter with a unit is only taken when the dump gives that unit.

VCA Comp.notes: The unit runs THRESHOLD -60 to +12 dB, ours -60 to 0, so a value above 0 is clamped and reported. Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e): the unit compresses from 1.28 dB below the threshold it shows (-1.23 to -1.36 over five takes at -20 and -30), hence the offset; RATIO matches exactly. ATTACK and RELEASE take the dump's real times (quad-cortex-curves.json), but the unit's envelope is shaped differently from ours, so the timing is close, not equal.

Legendary 87.notes: Closest is our FET Compressor. The unit's INPUT runs -48 to 0 dB and is anchored at the top (0 dB is our 40 dB of input), a guess. ATTACK is taken as ms and RELEASE as s. Our attack floor is 20 us and MAKEUP is our Output knob, -36 to 12 dB. Unverified.

Solid State Comp.notes: Closest is our Bus Compressor. Our attack and release are stepped (0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, 10, 30 ms; 0.1, 0.3, 0.6, 1.2 s, Auto) while the unit's are continuous, so only values on a step map and the rest are reported as dropped. Makeup is clamped to 0 to 24 dB. Unverified.

Opto Comp.notes: Closest is our Optical Compressor, one Peak Reduction knob and a programme-dependent cell. THRESHOLD becomes Peak Reduction (-2 dB is 0, -52 dB is 100). RATIO, ATTACK and RELEASE have no counterpart and are dropped; switch to Limit by hand for ratios of about 8 and above. Unverified.

Chief CS3.notes: Closest is our Sustainer. Knobs 0 to 10 become 0 to 100 %; LEVEL 0 to 10 becomes -18 to +12 dB (6 is unity). Our makeup is automatic and our attack and tone curves are our own. Unverified.

Jewel.notes: Nearest by controls is our Sustainer (comp, tone, level, mix). HIGH CUT has no counterpart and is dropped. A guess at the circuit. Unverified.

Ambience.notes: SIZE (a list of three) is our Small, Medium, Large in that order; HIGH PASS is our low cut and LOW PASS our high cut. Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified.

Modulated.notes: HIGH PASS is our low cut and LOW PASS our high cut. Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified.

Cave.notes: HIGH PASS is our low cut and LOW PASS our high cut. Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified.

Nordic Concert Hall.notes: All fifteen settings have a counterpart on our Large Hall. HIGH PASS is our low cut and LOW PASS our high cut; REV ATTACK is our Attack (0 starts at once, 100 swells in over a third of a second, which is our reading of it). Settings names and ranges from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified.

Studio Plate 70.notes: The unit gives it the same fifteen settings as its hall, and only our Large Hall has them all (bass multiplier and crossover, high shelf, both diffusions, attack); our Plate has none of those, so a plate preset placed there would lose most of its knobs. A plate is a short, dense, bright decay with no reflections: a small SIZE and high diffusions on the Large Hall get close, the imported values decide. Settings names and ranges from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified.

Blossom.notes: DUCKING in percent becomes our Duck in dB (100% is 24 dB), the release stays at its default. EXTRA E.R. and E.R. LENGTH (early reflections) have no counterpart and are reported as dropped. Settings names and ranges from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified.

Vintage Digital.notes: The unit gives DECAY in percent: mapped onto our 0.3 to 15 s range as a guess. Our word length (the grain) stays at its default. Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified.

Simple Gate.notes: Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified.

Utility Gate.notes: Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified. THRESHOLD measured on a unit (CorOS d14e, plan v14) with a sine: the real threshold in dBFS peak is 1.155 x setting - 10.95, fitted on settings -20, -30, -40 and -50 (setting -60 gave about -80). Our gate's detector follows the peaks of the waveform, so the peak law is used as it is (an RMS detector would take an offset of -13.96); results below our -80 are clamped and reported.

Graphic 9.notes: Measured on a unit: band gains are the dB the unit shows, 1:1. The 65 Hz band is a low shelf and the 16 kHz band a high shelf (our 63 Hz band, with its corner at 65 Hz in the Shelved ends style), 125 Hz to 8 kHz are peaking at the nominal centres; our 31.5 Hz band stays flat. Q is the unit's Q control, 0 to 10, value = Q (default 1), for every band. HPF (19 to 500 Hz) and LPF (1000 to 20001 Hz) are second-order filters of Q 1.0 whose corner is lo + span * n ^ (5/3), n being the knob position 0..1; the dump gives the knob on its linear scale and the table applies the curve. The unit's filters have no switch, so ours are switched on. Names of the Q and filter controls assumed; scaling measured.

Parametric-3.notes: Measured on a unit (wire values 0..1): GAIN is -12 + 24 * wire dB (0.5 is flat), Q is 0.1 + 9.9 * wire, FREQ is 20 + 19980 * wire ^ (10/3) Hz (the dump gives the knob on its linear 20 to 20000 scale and the table applies the curve), TYPE is peaking, high-pass, low-pass, high shelf, low shelf for wire 0, .25, .5, .75, 1 (the pass types are second order), and BYPASS 0 is a band that is off. Every band can take any of the five types, which our per-band shape control carries. The defaults are the unit's as loaded: low shelf at 125 Hz, peak at 1000 Hz, high shelf at 4000 Hz. Names of the type and bypass options assumed (the numbers 0 to 4 and the usual names are read).

Parametric-8.notes: Same laws as the Parametric-3 for every band (gain -12 + 24 * wire dB, Q 0.1 + 9.9 * wire, FREQ 20 + 19980 * wire ^ (10/3) Hz, five types, BYPASS 0 is off). As loaded: band 1 low shelf at 50 Hz, band 2 peaking at 100 Hz, band 4 high shelf at 1 kHz, band 5 peaking at 3 kHz, all Q 0.71, and bands 5 and 8 bypassed. Band 8 is a second-order low-pass with a fixed Q of 0.707 (its Q control does nothing), so its Q is not read and ours is held at 0.7071.

Low-High Cut.notes: The slope lists' option labels are not known yet: the map assumes 0 (off), 6, 12, 18, 24, 36 and 48 dB/oct; any other label is reported as dropped. Names and ranges from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified.

Plugin Parametric-4.notes: Measured on a unit: gains are the dB the unit shows, 1:1. All four bands are peaking with a fixed Q (LO 0.46, LO MID 0.50, HI MID 0.54, HI 0.58), which our Peaking band style holds. FREQ follows a table of the knob position (0, .1, .25, .5, .75, .9, 1) joined in the logarithm of the frequency: LO 20.1, 21.6, 28, 60, 100, 160, 200; LO MID 100, 108, 140, 260, 500, 680, 1000; HI MID 500, 540, 700, 1200, 3000, 4200, 5000; HI 2000, 2160, 2800, 6000, 12000, 16818, 20000 Hz. HPF (20 to 500 Hz) and LPF (1000 to 20000 Hz) are Butterworth (Q 0.707) and linear in the knob, as the dump gives them. The unit's filters have no switch, so ours are switched on.

Digital Delay.notes: Names and units from a unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e), as Digital Delay (M) and (ST): DELAY TIME 7 to 6000 ms, SYNC on by default (then the time follows SYNC NOTE), FEEDBACK and MIX in percent. Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e): its delay is 0.6 ms shorter than the time it shows, the same at 100, 500 and 1000 ms, hence the offset. DYN DEPTH (0 to 60 dB on the unit, clamped to our 24) and RELEASE become the ducking of the repeats; the unit's ducking is not measured against ours. SYNC NOTE arrives as an index into the unit's note list, measured on a unit (CorOS d14e) at 120 BPM, every note within 2.3 ms of its nominal time: 0 1/64T, 1 1/64, 2 1/32T, 3 1/64 dotted, 4 1/32, 5 1/16T, 6 1/32 dotted, 7 1/16, 8 1/8T, 9 1/16 dotted, 10 1/8, 11 1/4T, 12 1/8 dotted, 13 1/4, 14 1/2T, 15 1/4 dotted, 16 1/2, 17 1/1T, 18 1/2 dotted, 19 1/1, 20 1/1 dotted. Ours has no 1/64 notes, so 0, 1 and 3 are not in the map and are reported as dropped.

Analog Delay.notes: Time, feedback and mix; the time is DELAY TIME in milliseconds (name assumed from the Digital Delay). Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e, plan v13): with SYNC off it plays min + span * wire^(5/3) of the knob range (see quad-cortex-curves.json), so the dump script converts the wire value on that curve and the shown time arrives here in milliseconds. DYN DEPTH (0 to 60 dB on the unit, clamped to our 24) and RELEASE become the ducking of the repeats; the unit's ducking is not measured against ours.

Tape Delay.notes: Time, feedback and mix; wow, flutter and drive are not mapped. The time is DELAY TIME in milliseconds (name assumed from the Digital Delay). Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e, plan v13): with SYNC off it plays min + span * wire^(5/3) of the knob range (see quad-cortex-curves.json), so the dump script converts the wire value on that curve and the shown time arrives here in milliseconds. DYN DEPTH (0 to 60 dB on the unit, clamped to our 24) and RELEASE become the ducking of the repeats; the unit's ducking is not measured against ours.

Simple Delay.notes: Time, feedback and mix; the time is DELAY TIME in milliseconds (name assumed from the Digital Delay). Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e, plan v13): with SYNC off it plays min + span * wire^(5/3) of the knob range (see quad-cortex-curves.json), so the dump script converts the wire value on that curve and the shown time arrives here in milliseconds. DYN DEPTH (0 to 60 dB on the unit, clamped to our 24) and RELEASE become the ducking of the repeats; the unit's ducking is not measured against ours.

Slapback Delay.notes: From a unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e): DELAY TIME 40 to 200 ms, FEEDBACK and MIX in percent, LOW PASS and HIGH PASS in Hz. LOW PASS becomes our tone sweep; HIGH PASS has no counterpart here and is dropped, and the saturation and wobble are ours and stay at their defaults. A FEEDBACK above our 60% is clamped and reported. DYN DEPTH (0 to 60 dB, clamped to our 24) and RELEASE become the ducking. DELAY TIME is 40 to 200 ms. Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e, plan v13): with SYNC off it plays min + span * wire^(5/3) of the knob range (see quad-cortex-curves.json), so the dump script converts the wire value on that curve and the shown time arrives here in milliseconds. SYNC NOTE is the Digital Delay's note list cut to indices 0 to 10 (1/64T to 1/8), measured on a unit (CorOS d14e); the unit then clamps the time to its 40 to 200 ms, so at 120 BPM its 1/8 plays 200 ms where ours plays the full 250 ms. Ours has no 1/64 notes, so 0, 1 and 3 are reported as dropped.

Dual Delay.notes: From a unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e): DELAY TIME L and R 7 to 6000 ms, FEEDBACK L and R and X-FEEDBACK in percent, HIGH PASS 20 to 800 Hz and LOW PASS 1000 to 16000 Hz (the L and R names are the catalogue's wording, not yet seen in a dump). HIGH PASS is our low cut and LOW PASS our high cut. DYN DEPTH (0 to 60 dB, clamped to our 24) and RELEASE become the ducking. DELAY TIME L and R follow the same law. Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e, plan v13): with SYNC off each plays min + span * wire^(5/3) of the knob range (see quad-cortex-curves.json), so the dump script converts the wire value on that curve and the shown times arrive here in milliseconds.

Reverse Delay.notes: From a unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e): DELAY TIME 20 to 4000 ms (ours is 100 to 2000, so a value outside is clamped and reported), FEEDBACK and MIX in percent, HIGH PASS and LOW PASS in Hz. LOW PASS becomes our tone; HIGH PASS has no counterpart here and is dropped. DELAY TIME follows the same law. Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e, plan v13): with SYNC off it plays min + span * wire^(5/3) of the knob range (see quad-cortex-curves.json), so the dump script converts the wire value on that curve and the shown time arrives here in milliseconds.

Dual Reverse Delay.notes: From a unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e): DELAY TIME L and R, FEEDBACK L and R and X-FEEDBACK in percent, HIGH PASS and LOW PASS in Hz (the L and R names are the catalogue's wording, not yet seen in a dump). Placed on our dual reverse delay: a reverse line per side, each with its own time and feedback, and X-FEEDBACK as the share of each line's repeats that crosses to the other. HIGH PASS is our low cut and LOW PASS our tone. DELAY TIME L and R follow the same law. Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e, plan v13): with SYNC off it plays min + span * wire^(5/3) of the knob range (see quad-cortex-curves.json), so the dump script converts the wire value on that curve and the shown time arrives here in milliseconds.

Circular Delay.notes: Placed on our multi-tap delay, a diffused cluster of repeats. From a unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e): DELAY TIME 27 to 2000 ms, FEEDBACK 0 to 95 %, DIFFUSION and MIX in percent, HIGH PASS and LOW PASS in Hz. HIGH PASS is our low cut and LOW PASS our high cut. The tap count and pattern are ours and stay at their defaults. Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e, plan v13): DELAY TIME with SYNC off is linear in the wire value, so it is taken as milliseconds as it is. The sound is a neighbour of the unit's, not a copy.

Simple Ping Pong Delay.notes: Time, feedback and mix (DELAY TIME name assumed from the Digital Delay). Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e, plan v13): with SYNC off it plays min + span * wire^(5/3) of the knob range (see quad-cortex-curves.json), so the dump script converts the wire value on that curve and the shown time arrives here in milliseconds. Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e, plan v13): the right side repeats at twice the time of the left, which our ping pong ratio choices (1:1, dotted, golden) cannot express, so the right line stays on its ratio.

Room.notes: Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified. DECAY scaled from one unit measurement (CorOS d14e, DECAY 1 s): the unit's burst T60 is 0.65 s.

Hall.notes: Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified. DECAY scaled from one unit measurement (CorOS d14e, DECAY 3 s): the unit's burst T60 is 1.65 s.

Plate.notes: The unit gives DECAY in percent: mapped onto our 0.5 to 10 s range as a guess. Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified. DECAY scaled from one unit measurement (CorOS d14e, DECAY 50 %): the unit's burst T60 is 1.59 s; other values follow the line through it.

Plate Lush.notes: The unit gives DECAY in percent: mapped onto our 0.5 to 10 s range as a guess. Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified. DECAY scaled from one unit measurement (CorOS d14e, DECAY 50 %): the unit's burst T60 is 2.60 s; other values follow the line through it.

Plate Tight.notes: The unit gives DECAY in percent: mapped onto our 0.5 to 10 s range as a guess. Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified.

Shimmer.notes: Its FEEDBACK (how much of the shifted sound returns) drives our Shimmer amount; PITCH stays at our octave. Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified.

Spring.notes: BOING, how hard the springs are struck, maps onto our Dwell. Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified.

Vintage Chorus.notes: Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified.

Chorus Engine.notes: DEPTH follows the unit's law, measured on a unit: the pitch moves by about 3 cents (peak to peak, at 1 Hz) at DEPTH 50 and 10 cents at 100, a curve of the knob to the 1.75 power; our depth is a straight line, so it is 20.4 x (DEPTH / 100) ^ 1.75 percent. Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); the rest of the scaling ours, unverified.

Digital Flanger.notes: Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified.

Flanger Engine.notes: Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified.

Flangerish.notes: Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified.

Phaser.notes: On our lifted voicing, made for MIX 50: the unit's response is lifted by +1.5 to +5.7 dB from 50 Hz to 16 kHz where the classic voicing dips to -5 dB. SPEED is a 0 to 100 knob, not Hz, so the rate stays at ours until it is timed on a unit. Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified.

Tremolo.notes: Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified.

Vibrato.notes: On our delay excursion depth mode: DEPTH in percent is the size of the delay sweep (100 is 2 ms either side), measured on a unit as 21.7 cents peak to peak per Hz of RATE at DEPTH 50. Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified.

Rotary.notes: On our dark cabinet (24 dB down at 8 kHz, 50 dB at 16 kHz, as on the unit) and the unit's speeds: its drum turns at 0.71 Hz slow and 4.15 Hz fast, which is a horn of 4.85 Hz and a slow speed of 17.1 percent of fast. SPEED is the slow and fast switch: 0 slow, 1 fast, as ours. Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified.

Envelope Filter.notes: SENS (18 to 54 dB) is spread over our 0 to 100 % and RESO (1 to 10) over our resonance. Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified.

Auto Wah.notes: The unit's auto wah follows the playing, so it maps onto our envelope filter. Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified.

Crying Wah.notes: WAH is the pedal position, 0 to 1. Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified.

Crying Clyde Wah.notes: WAH is the pedal position, 0 to 1. Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified.

Bubba Wah.notes: WAH is the pedal position, 0 to 1. Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified.

Bass Wah.notes: WAH is the pedal position, 0 to 1. Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified.

Bad Horse.notes: WAH is the pedal position, 0 to 1. Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified.

Crying Wah From Hell.notes: WAH is the pedal position, 0 to 1; its range, Q and boost stay at ours. Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified.

Pitch Shifter.notes: Fine past 50 cents either way is clamped to ours. Settings names from the unit's catalogue (CorOS d14e); scaling ours, unverified.

Poly Octaver.notes: Parameters not mapped: names unknown. Ours is not polyphonic.

Gain.notes: Names, ranges and units assumed (LEVEL -60 to +12 dB, PAN -1 to 1, PHASE INVERT a switch), not read from a dump. Ours runs -24 to +24 dB, so a level below -24 is clamped and reported. Our pan is a balance control on a stereo signal (-1 left to +1 right).

Volume.notes: Names assumed (LEVEL 0 to 100 %, a CURVE switch), not read from a dump. The floor stays at our default (silence at the heel). Our position is the pedal position, which the expression pedal drives.

Doubler.notes: Names and units assumed, not read from a dump. Our spread runs 3 to 60 ms and the levels -40 to +12 dB; values outside are clamped and reported. The doubling is our own design (a slowly moving short delay), so it is close in kind, not in sound.

Phase Doctor.notes: Only the polarity switch is mapped (name assumed). The other controls are dropped; set the delay by ear, 0 to 5 ms.

Myth Drive.notes: Closest is the transparent drive (a clean path plus a clipped path), on its smooth voicing, matched to the unit's response. Knob names are the unit's own (catalogue, CorOS d14e); the scaling is ours and unverified. LEVEL is set from unit measurements (CorOS d14e, LEVEL 5): first at GAIN 7, then re-measured at GAIN 5 at 30 dB below full scale, where the unit is about 5 dB louder than our 0 dB, hence the offset.

Obsessive Drive.notes: On our overdrive's heavy voicing (fully clipped, a large bass lift after the clipping), fitted to the unit. TONE runs on a curve so that 5 is the unit's top end (our 57 %). Knob names are the unit's own (catalogue, CorOS d14e). Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e): VOLUME is set so that 5 gives the unit's 1 kHz level with the other knobs at 5.

OD250.notes: Gain and volume, the pedal's two knobs. On our distortion's open voicing (hard clipping to a level that does not follow the input, a one-pole filter), which matches the unit's response and distortion. The unit is flat to the top, so our filter is fully open. Knob names are the unit's own (catalogue, CorOS d14e). Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e): VOLUME is set so that 5 gives the unit's 1 kHz level at GAIN 5.

Rodent Drive.notes: DISTORTION, FILTER and VOLUME are the pedal's three knobs, on our open voicing, matched to the unit's response. Its filter is a low-pass that darkens as it goes up, so it is inverted onto our Filter. Knob names are the unit's own (catalogue, CorOS d14e); the scaling is ours and unverified. VOLUME is set from a unit measurement (CorOS d14e, VOLUME 5): the unit sits 15.6 dB below our 0 dB at DISTORTION 3 and 7, hence the offset.

Green 808.notes: On our overdrive's focused voicing (a clean path plus a soft clipped, high-passed path), fitted to the unit with the mid hump family. OVERDRIVE runs on a curve (5 is our 33 %) so the distortion at 100 Hz follows the unit at 2, 5 and 8, where the level barely moves. Knob names are the unit's own (catalogue, CorOS d14e). Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e): LEVEL is set so that 5 gives the unit's 1 kHz level at OVERDRIVE 5.

Exotic.notes: On our boost's warm voicing (a soft clipped boost with a broad low lift and a darker top, the same clipping as the warm overdrive), fitted to the unit; GAIN (0 to 10) becomes 0 to 20 dB of our Gain, which drives the clipping. Knob names are the unit's own (catalogue, CorOS d14e). Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e): the voicing's own level gives the unit's 1 kHz level at GAIN 5, and like the unit it barely moves with GAIN.

Freeman BOD.notes: A high-gain drive with gain, bass, treble, presence, tight, trim and volume: our metal distortion fits best (presence and trim stay at our defaults). Knob names are the unit's own (catalogue, CorOS d14e); the scaling is ours and unverified. VOLUME is set from a unit measurement (CorOS d14e, VOLUME 5, other knobs at 5): the unit sits 13.7 dB below our 0 dB at 1 kHz, hence the offset.

Brit Blues.notes: On our overdrive's warm voicing (a clean path plus a soft clipped path, a broad lift below 500 Hz and a darker top), fitted to the unit. On the unit GAIN also raises the level (about 6 dB from 2 to 8); ours keeps it nearly fixed. Knob names are the unit's own (catalogue, CorOS d14e). Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e): VOLUME is set so that 5 gives the unit's 1 kHz level with the other knobs at 5.

Chief DS1.notes: Hard clipping distortion on our notched voicing (a lopsided clip, a bass lift and a narrow notch near 1 kHz), fitted to the unit: a 1 kHz note measures close to 100 % distortion and a 100 Hz one about a quarter of that. Its tone knob moves our top low-pass. Knob names are the unit's own (catalogue, CorOS d14e). Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e): LEVEL is set so that 5 gives the unit's 1 kHz level with the other knobs at 5.

Brit Governor.notes: A distortion with a three-band EQ: our metal distortion, its EQ at our fixed mid frequency. Knob names are the unit's own (catalogue, CorOS d14e); the scaling is ours and unverified. LEVEL is set from a unit measurement (CorOS d14e, LEVEL 5, other knobs at 5): the unit sits 10.2 dB below our 0 dB at 1 kHz, hence the offset.

Chief MT.notes: On our resonant voicing, matched to the unit's response. DIST, LOW, MIDDLE, MIDFREQ, HIGH and LEVEL on a 0 to 10 scale. The middle frequency becomes 200 Hz to 3 kHz and the three tone knobs 12 dB either way. Tight and the gate stay at our defaults. Knob names are the unit's own (catalogue, CorOS d14e); the scaling is ours and unverified. LEVEL is set from a unit measurement (CorOS d14e, DIST 6, LEVEL 5): the unit sits 21.5 dB below our 0 dB, hence the offset.

Chief OD1.notes: On our overdrive's focused voicing (a clean path plus a soft clipped, high-passed path), fitted to the unit with the mid hump family. GAIN runs on a steep curve (5 is our 7 %): the unit keeps its lows nearly clean until GAIN is high. Its tone is fixed; ours stays at the middle. Knob names are the unit's own (catalogue, CorOS d14e). Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e): LEVEL is set so that 5 gives the unit's 1 kHz level at GAIN 5.

Chief SD1.notes: On our overdrive's focused voicing (a clean path plus a soft clipped, high-passed path), fitted to the unit with the mid hump family. OVERDRIVE runs on a curve (5 is our 72 %): this pedal distorts more at 100 Hz than the others of the family. Knob names are the unit's own (catalogue, CorOS d14e). Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e): LEVEL is set so that 5 gives the unit's 1 kHz level at OVERDRIVE 5.

Fuzz Pi.notes: SUSTAIN, TONE and VOLUME, on the scooped voicing, matched to the unit's response. Knob names are the unit's own (catalogue, CorOS d14e); the scaling is ours and unverified. VOLUME is set from unit measurements (CorOS d14e, VOLUME 5): first at SUSTAIN 6, then re-measured at SUSTAIN 5, where the unit sits about 21.9 dB below our 0 dB, hence the offset.

Chief BD2.notes: On our overdrive's heavy voicing (fully clipped, a large bass lift after the clipping), fitted to the unit. TONE runs on a curve so that 5 is the unit's open top end (our 76 %). Knob names are the unit's own (catalogue, CorOS d14e). Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e): VOLUME is set so that 5 gives the unit's 1 kHz level with the other knobs at 5.

Rage Booster.notes: On our treble boost's cranked voicing (a high-pass into a clipping stage at a fixed drive), fitted to the unit, where the distortion does not move with VOLUME: VOLUME is the level after the clipping. It runs on a curve close to the unit's (about 8 dB from 2 to 5 and 4 dB from 5 to 8). Range and level stay at our defaults. Knob names are the unit's own (catalogue, CorOS d14e). Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e): the curve gives the unit's 1 kHz level at VOLUME 5.

Facial Fuzz.notes: FUZZ and VOLUME, on our open fuzz voicing (a hard, lopsided clip with an open top), fitted to the unit; the pedal has no tone knob, so ours sits where the unit's top end is (91 %). Knob names are the unit's own (catalogue, CorOS d14e). Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e): VOLUME is set so that 5 gives the unit's 1 kHz level with FUZZ at 5.

Exotic Z Boost.notes: On our boost's hot voicing (a low cut into a soft clipper), fitted to the unit: clean at a low GAIN, clipping gently from the middle up, its level rising less and less with GAIN as on the unit. GAIN (0 to 10) becomes 0 to 20 dB. Knob names are the unit's own (catalogue, CorOS d14e). Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e): the voicing's own level gives the unit's 1 kHz level at GAIN 5.

Red Drive.notes: On our overdrive's focused voicing (a clean path plus a soft clipped, high-passed path), fitted to the unit with the mid hump family. Knob names are the unit's own (catalogue, CorOS d14e). Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e): LEVEL is set so that 5 gives the unit's 1 kHz level at DRIVE 5.

Vemural Ray.notes: On our overdrive's warm voicing (a clean path plus a soft clipped path, a broad lift below 500 Hz and a darker top), fitted to the unit. TREBLE moves our tone low-pass. Knob names are the unit's own (catalogue, CorOS d14e). Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e): LEVEL is set so that 5 gives the unit's 1 kHz level with the other knobs at 5.

No-Bell OD1.notes: On our overdrive's heavy voicing (fully clipped, a large bass lift after the clipping), fitted to the unit. SPECTRUM runs on a curve so that 5 is the unit's darker top end (our 24 %). Knob names are the unit's own (catalogue, CorOS d14e). Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e): LEVEL is set so that 5 gives the unit's 1 kHz level with the other knobs at 5.

Thunderpaw.notes: Distortion, with the tone knob onto our Filter. On our distortion's open voicing (hard clipping to a level that does not follow the input, a one-pole filter), which matches the unit's response and distortion. Knob names are the unit's own (catalogue, CorOS d14e). Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e): OUTPUT is set so that 5 gives the unit's 1 kHz level with the other knobs at 5.

MK3 Silicon Fuzz.notes: On our open fuzz voicing (a hard, lopsided clip with an open top), fitted to the unit. Knob names are the unit's own (catalogue, CorOS d14e). Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e): LEVEL is set so that 5 gives the unit's 1 kHz level with the other knobs at 5.

81 Creations Drive.notes: Drive, cut and output. On our distortion's open voicing (hard clipping to a level that does not follow the input, a one-pole filter), which matches the unit's response and distortion. CUT darkens as it goes up, so it is inverted onto our Filter. Knob names are the unit's own (catalogue, CorOS d14e). Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e): OUTPUT is set so that 0 dB gives the unit's 1 kHz level at DRV 50.

BDDI.notes: On our bass drive's DI voicing (a nearly clean preamp with a fixed low and presence lift), fitted to the unit, which stays clean at bass level while DRIVE raises its gain. BLEND at 5 is the fitted mix. Knob names are the unit's own (catalogue, CorOS d14e). Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e): LEVEL is set so that 5 gives the unit's 1 kHz level with the other knobs at 5.

Douglas MT 3K.notes: On our bass drive's grit voicing (a clean path plus a clipped, high-passed path), fitted to the unit, with the crossover at 800 Hz so the lows stay clean as they do on the unit. DRIVE runs on a curve (5 is our 64 %). BLEND at 5 is the fitted mix. Knob names are the unit's own (catalogue, CorOS d14e). Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e): LEVEL is set so that 5 gives the unit's 1 kHz level with the other knobs at 5.

Douglas Vintage MT.notes: On our bass drive's grit voicing (a clean path plus a clipped, high-passed path), fitted to the unit. DRIVE runs on a curve (5 is our 37 %). BLEND at 5 is the fitted mix. Knob names are the unit's own (catalogue, CorOS d14e). Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e): LEVEL is set so that 5 gives the unit's 1 kHz level with the other knobs at 5.

Soviet Fuzz.notes: A bass fuzz, on our thick fuzz voicing (two clipping stages and a very large bass lift), fitted to the unit. Knob names are the unit's own (catalogue, CorOS d14e). Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e): VOLUME is set so that 5 gives the unit's 1 kHz level with the other knobs at 5.

Exotic Bass Z Boost.notes: On our bass drive's boost voicing (a low cut and a soft top into a soft clipper), fitted to the unit: clean at bass level, clipping gently when pushed, the level following GAIN as on the unit. Knob names are the unit's own (catalogue, CorOS d14e). Measured on a unit (CorOS d14e): VOLUME is set so that 5 gives the unit's 1 kHz level at GAIN 5.
